t: In the motor insurance contract, the 'second party' is:
o: The driver of the insured vehicle
e: First party is the insured, second party the insurer, and the third party is any person who suffers injury, death or property damage from the use of the insured vehicle.

t: One of the stated aims of the 2019 amendment was to increase the time limit for renewal of a driving licence from one month to:
o: Six months before and after expiry
One year before and after expiry
e: The amendment enlarged the renewal window from one month to one year before and after the expiry date, besides raising transport licence validity from three to five years.

t: The provisions of the 2019 amendment relating to investigation of accidents and settlement of claims (the detailed accident report scheme) were implemented from:
e: The Act came into force on 1 September 2019, but the CMV Rules for investigation and settlement of claims (Rule 150A and the Forms) were brought into effect from 1 April 2022.

t: Third party insurance and the Claims Tribunals are dealt with in which Chapters and Sections of the MV Act?
o: Chapters XIII and XIV, Sections 177 to 217
Chapters XI and XII, Sections 145 to 176
e: Chapter XI (Insurance of motor vehicles against third party risks) and Chapter XII (Claims Tribunals) span Sections 145 to 176.

t: The pre-amendment Section 149 (duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards) is now renumbered as:
e: The old s.149 became s.150 with added defences; a new s.149 on settlement by the insurer and procedure therefor was inserted.

t: The Hit and Run Compensation Fund within the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund is sourced from:
o: The balance under the Solatium Scheme, 1989 and a notified percentage of total third party premium collected by general insurers
e: The Hit and Run Compensation Fund takes the Solatium Scheme balance and a Central Government-notified percentage of TP premium; it is administered by GIC under the supervision of MoRTH.

t: The Account for Uninsured Vehicles / Hit and Run Accidents of the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund can be credited with:
o: National Highway user fees, budgetary grants from the Consolidated Fund of India and fines under Section 198A
Own damage premium collected by insurers
e: Rules under s.164B list user fees, Consolidated Fund grants, s.198A fines and other notified sources for the uninsured/hit-and-run account; insurers fund the insured-vehicles account.

t: Under Section 166, an application for compensation may be made by:
o: The injured person, the owner of damaged property, the legal representatives of the deceased, or a duly authorised agent
The investigating police officer on behalf of the victim
The insurer of the offending vehicle
e: Section 166(1) lists the injured person, the owner of the property, all or any legal representatives where death has resulted, and any agent duly authorised by them.

t: Before the 2019 amendment, no appeal lay against a Tribunal award if the amount in dispute was less than:
e: The threshold was ten thousand rupees; the amendment raised it to one lakh rupees to reduce frivolous appeals.

t: After the 2019 amendment, a driving licence for a transport vehicle carrying goods of dangerous or hazardous nature is valid for:
e: Hazardous-goods licence validity was raised from one year to three years; ordinary transport licences from three to five years.

t: The compensation for death in a hit-and-run motor accident under the amended Section 161 is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2019 amendment raised hit-and-run compensation from ₹25,000 to ₹2,00,000 for death and from ₹12,500 to ₹50,000 for grievous hurt.

t: After the amendment, a non-transport driving licence issued to a person below 30 years of age is valid:
e: Age-banded validity: below 30 – till age 40; 30 to below 50 – 10 years; 50 to below 55 – till age 60; 55 and above – 5 years.

t: Under the MV Act, a 'heavy goods vehicle' is a goods carriage whose gross vehicle weight exceeds:
e: Heavy goods vehicle: GVW above 12,000 kg (or road-roller/tractor with ULW above 12,000 kg); medium: 7,501–12,000 kg; light: up to 7,500 kg.

t: Under Section 2 of the MV Act, 'goods' carried in a vehicle:
o: Includes cattle but excludes living persons and equipment ordinarily used with the vehicle
Means only manufactured articles for sale
e: 'Goods' means anything carried other than equipment ordinarily used with the vehicle and living persons, and expressly includes cattle (livestock).

t: Under Section 128, the driver of a two-wheeled motorcycle shall not carry more than:
o: Two persons in addition to himself
One person in addition to himself
e: Section 128 restricts a two-wheeler to the rider plus one pillion; violation attracts penalty under s.194C and may be treated as contributory negligence in a claim.

t: Which pair correctly matches the old IPC section with its BNS 2023 counterpart?
e: 302 IPC → 101 BNS; 379 IPC → 303 BNS; 304A IPC → 106 BNS; 337 IPC → 125(a) BNS; 338 IPC → 125(b) BNS; 279 IPC → 281 BNS.

t: After the 2019 amendment, an application for compensation under Section 166 must be made within:
o: Six months of the occurrence of the accident
Ninety days of the occurrence of the accident
Twelve months of the occurrence of the accident
Two years of the occurrence of the accident
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The amended s.166(3) reintroduced a limitation of six months from the accident; under the pre-amendment law there was no time limit for filing a claim petition.

t: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation was decided by the Supreme Court on:
e: Sarla Verma (15.04.2009) laid down the three-step method (multiplicand, multiplier, calculation) and the standardised multiplier table later approved in Pranay Sethi.

t: The multiplier table in Sarla Verma was prepared by harmonising which earlier Supreme Court decisions?
o: Kaushnuma Begum, Minu Mehta and Rambha Devi
Rajesh v. Rajbir, Reshma Kumari and Pranay Sethi
Challa Bharathamma, Mukund Dewangan and Nanu Ram
Susamma Thomas, Trilok Chandra and Charlie
e: Sarla Verma applied the Susamma Thomas, Trilok Chandra and Charlie decisions to arrive at the standard multiplier table.

t: The multiplier for a deceased aged 66 to 70 years is:
e: The table ends at M-5 for 66–70 years (M-7 for 61–65, M-9 for 56–60).

t: Under Section 196 of the amended MV Act, driving an uninsured vehicle attracts for the first offence:
o: Imprisonment up to 1 year and/or fine of ₹10,000
Imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine of ₹2,000
e: Section 196: first offence – imprisonment up to three months or fine of ₹2,000 or both; subsequent offence – fine ₹4,000 (earlier ₹1,000).

topic: Third party – who is a third party
t: A stage carriage bus with a registered capacity of 52 carries 50 passengers; the bus falls into a gorge due to the driver's negligence, killing 20. Under the Act policy, the passengers are:
o: Covered only under the compulsory PA cover
Covered only up to ₹5 lakh each under Section 164 with no further claim
Not third parties, since they contracted with the bus owner
Third parties whose death is covered under Section 147 as passengers of a transport vehicle
e: Section 147(1)(b)(ii) covers death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle (except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle) up to registered capacity.

t: Which constitutional provision underpins the Lok Adalat system of alternative dispute resolution?
o: Article 39-A (equal justice and free legal aid)
e: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 implements the mandate of Article 39-A of the Constitution by providing free legal aid and Lok Adalats.

t: An insurer's designated officer wishes to settle a death claim directly with the family outside the Tribunal and obtain a discharge. Under Section 149 the offer:
o: May be made privately and is binding without Tribunal involvement
Should be made to the claimant before the Claims Tribunal, which records the settlement as a consent settlement
Can be made only after the Tribunal passes an award
Must be routed through the Insurance Ombudsman
e: Section 149(2)–(3) contemplates the offer being made before the Claims Tribunal; on acceptance the Tribunal records the settlement and the claim is deemed settled by consent.

t: Under the detailed accident report scheme, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle must furnish their particulars (Forms III and IV) to the Investigating Officer within:
e: Driver's Form III and owner's Form IV go to the IO within 30 days; the victim's Forms VI-A and VI-B within 60 days.

t: Where the insurer accepts liability in Form XI and the amount offered is fair and acceptable to the claimants, the Tribunal passes a consent award. The proceedings are to be completed within:
e: Consent award – six months; dispute on quantum only – nine months; liability contested – inquiry to be completed within twelve months of the accident.

t: An insured private car is used by its owner in an organised car rally involving speed testing on public roads and crashes into a shop. Under Section 150(2) the insurer:
o: Can defend only if the owner had no licence
Must pay without any defence as third party property is involved
Can defend on the ground of breach of the condition excluding organised racing and speed testing
Has no defence, since the owner himself was driving
e: Use for organised racing and speed testing is one of the specified use-related breaches that the insurer may plead under s.150(2)(a)(i).

t: The compensation under Section 161 for hit-and-run victims is administered by:
o: The State Government from the Consolidated Fund of the State
IRDAI from the policyholders' protection fund
GIC as the nodal agency, under the supervision of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, from the Hit and Run Compensation Fund
The Claims Tribunal from court deposits
e: The Hit and Run Compensation Fund of the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund is administered by GIC under MoRTH's supervision; a Central Government scheme (2022) governs claims.

t: Under Section 185 of the MV Act, a person is deemed to be driving under the influence of alcohol if the blood alcohol level exceeds:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 185 fixes the limit at 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood detected by a breath analyser (or other prescribed test). Drunken driving is also a specified defence for the insurer under s.150(2).

t: Compare the deleted Sections 140–144 with the new Section 164. Which statement is correct?
o: Sections 140–144 gave interim no-fault relief (₹50,000 death / ₹25,000 permanent disablement) adjustable against the final award; Section 164 gives a higher, fixed and final no-fault compensation
Section 140 required proof of negligence while Section 164 does not
Both provide interim relief adjustable against a Section 166 award
Section 164 merely raised the Section 140 amounts without changing their interim nature
e: Old Chapter X provided interim no-fault relief adjustable against the final award; s.164 provides fixed (₹5 lakh / ₹2.5 lakh) compensation which is full and final.

t: A claimant files a Section 166 petition without pleading negligence of the driver and leads no evidence on it. The insurer objects. The Tribunal:
o: Must refer the case to the police for investigation
Must dismiss or reject the claim under Section 166, since fault liability requires negligence to be pleaded and proved; the claimant could instead have invoked Section 164
Must award compensation, since negligence is presumed in all motor accidents
e: Section 166 is a fault-based remedy; negligence must be pleaded and proved. Section 164 is the no-fault route with fixed amounts.

t: Before the 2019 amendment, the limitation for filing a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal was:
e: The limitation (originally six months, extendable) had been deleted by the 1994 amendment; the 2019 amendment reintroduced a six-month limit under s.166(3).

t: A fleet owner replaces an old bus with a new one of the same type and wants to continue operating on his existing route. Under the MV Act:
o: The permit is personal to the vehicle and cannot be replaced
Only a temporary permit under Section 87 can be given
A fresh permit must be obtained and the old permit lapses
The permit can be transferred from the old vehicle to the replacement vehicle of the same nature under Section 83
e: Section 83 permits the replacement of a vehicle covered by a permit with another vehicle of the same nature, subject to the authority's approval.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: A private car registered in 2010 completes 15 years in 2025. Its registration can be renewed for a period of:
e: After the initial 15-year validity, renewal of registration of a private (non-transport) vehicle is granted for five years at a time under Sections 41 and 56 read with the CMV Rules.

t: A driving licence expired in January 2023 and the holder applies for renewal in June 2024. Under Section 15 he must:
o: Undergo a fresh driving test, as more than one year has elapsed since expiry
Obtain a fresh learner's licence and wait 30 days only
e: Where renewal is sought more than one year after expiry, a fresh test of competence is required; within the one-year grace period only the fee/late fee applies.

t: Pranay Sethi extended standardised future prospects to which category that Sarla Verma had left uncertain?
o: Self-employed persons and persons on fixed salary
e: Sarla Verma confined future prospects to salaried permanent employees; Pranay Sethi extended them to self-employed/fixed-salary persons at 40%, 25% and 10%.

t: In the Challa Bharathamma case, the Supreme Court interpreted 'owner of the goods' under Section 147 to mean:
o: The consignee named in the lorry receipt, even if not travelling
The person who owned the goods and was travelling with them in the cabin of the goods vehicle
Any passenger carried in the goods vehicle
The driver of the goods vehicle
e: Only the owner of the goods (or his authorised representative) actually travelling with the goods is covered; other persons in a goods vehicle are gratuitous passengers and excluded.

t: Under the amended Section 185, the punishment for a first offence of drunken driving is:
o: Imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine up to ₹15,000
Imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine up to ₹10,000
e: Section 185: first offence – imprisonment up to six months and/or fine up to ₹10,000; second offence within three years – imprisonment up to two years and/or fine ₹15,000.

t: A 41-year-old permanent government employee earning ₹60,000 per month dies leaving wife, two children and mother. Loss of dependency is:
A 22-year-old unmarried self-employed delivery agent earning ₹10,000 per month dies in 2024; his parents are the dependants. Total compensation including conventional heads (+20%) is:
e: 1,20,000 + 40% = 1,68,000; bachelor with only parents → deduct 1/2 = 84,000; × 18 = 15,12,000. Add filial consortium 48,000 × 2, estate 18,000, funeral 18,000 = 1,32,000. Total ₹16,44,000.

t: A self-employed deceased aged 55 earning ₹20,000 per month leaves his wife and mother as dependants. Loss of dependency is:
Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

t: A 45-year-old salaried employee earning ₹30,000 per month suffers 100% functional disability (paraplegia) in an accident. Compensation for loss of future earnings, applying 30% future prospects, is:
e: 3,60,000 + 30% = 4,68,000 annual loss (100% disability, no personal-expense deduction in injury cases) × multiplier 14 (41–45) = ₹65,52,000.

t: A married deceased leaves wife, four children, parents and a dependent unmarried sister (eight dependants). The deduction for personal expenses is:
e: More than six dependants → deduction of 1/5 under Pranay Sethi.

t: An award of ₹30,00,000 carries 7.5% simple interest for 18 months, shared equally by three claimants with PAN. Net interest paid to each claimant after TDS is:
A deceased leaves wife, two children and both parents (five claimants) in a 2025 accident. Consortium alone under Pranay Sethi read with Magma v. Nanu Ram (+20%) totals:
e: Each eligible claimant (spousal, parental × 2, filial × 2) gets 48,000 (40,000 + 20%): 48,000 × 5 = ₹2,40,000.

t: A Tribunal awards ₹1,20,000 compensation. The owner wishes to appeal, disputing the whole award. The deposit required is:
e: The amount in dispute exceeds ₹1 lakh so an appeal lies; deposit is the lesser of ₹25,000 and 50% (₹60,000), i.e. ₹25,000.

t: A claimant received ₹1,00,000 interim relief under a State scheme for a death and then claims under Section 164. The amount payable under Section 164 is:
e: Section 164 provides ₹5,00,000 for death, less compensation already paid under any other law or scheme for the same accident: 5,00,000 − 1,00,000 = ₹4,00,000.

t: A 37-year-old permanent employee earning ₹24,000 per month dies leaving a wife and three children. Loss of dependency is:
